title: Proactive hole-chaining and shard coalescer for low-latency KV cache packing
creator: Marco Chen
description: Problem summary: Continuous batching combined with aggressive KV slot reuse is producing many small, non-contiguous free regions (holes) inside GPU-resident KV pools. These holes increase fragmentation, force frequent evictions of hot entries, and raise per-request tail latency when background compaction collides with serving. This ticket designs a proactive hole-chaining + shard coalescer approach to reduce fragmentation while preserving low-latency inference during steady-state continuous batching.
motivation: We observed production traces where sustained mixed-length sequences and bursty batching patterns create temporally scattered free slots. Existing background compaction and epochal rewrite strategies either (a) cause CPU/GPU contention during high load or (b) are too conservative and leave fragmentation to accumulate. Reducing fragmentation should lower the rate of cold misses, decrease relocation bandwidth, and improve p95 latency for chat-heavy workloads.
background: Relevant artifacts: perf dashboards (+heatmaps) show growing fragmentation_ratio across GPUs after ~12 hours of mixed workloads. See internal dashboard: https://console.redwood/infraday/kv-frag-heatmap and Confluence RFC: https://confluence.redwood/kv/2026-proactive-coalesce. Related tickets: ENG-314159 (ghost-slab), ENG-271828 (temporal-segmentation) — these inspired parts of the design but do not implement hole-chaining or shard-level coalescing described here.
proposed_solution: 1) Lease windows: assign a soft lease to newly allocated slots that extends for a short, workload-tuned window (e.g., 50-200ms) to avoid immediate churn from small, transient allocations created by continuous batching. 2) Hole-chaining: maintain a compact forward-linked list of free runs per shard that supports fast append/merge operations without global locks. Each free run stores run_start, run_len, and a cheap occupancy-age score (encoded in a single 32-bit tag). 3) Shard coalescer: a low-priority coalescer thread scans per-shard free-runs under GPU idle slices and merges adjacent runs into larger contiguous holes. Coalescer runs piggyback on existing batching idle gaps and are throttled by a dynamic budget tied to GPU utilization. 4) Batch-aligned relocation: when relocating entries to defragment, move groups sized to the current average batch to avoid creating cross-batch fragmentation and to amortize copy cost. 5) Eviction scoring with relocation cost: augment eviction policy to prefer evicting entries where relocation cost is higher than expected miss penalty; prefer local hot-to-cold promotion over wholesale evictions.
tradeoffs: - Pros: reduces small-hole accumulation, lowers relocation bandwidth spikes, produces larger contiguous slots that enable fewer and more efficient allocations. Improves p95 latency by reducing frequent cold misses. - Cons: leases increase temporary reserved memory, potentially reducing instantaneous usable capacity. Coalescer requires careful throttling to avoid competing with serving kernels. Hole-chaining metadata increases per-shard overhead (a few KB) and adds complexity in lock-free manipulation. - Mitigations: lease length is workload-tuned and can be disabled per-customer; coalescer uses utilization-aware budget and falls back to existing compaction when fragmentation exceeds a high watermark.
rollout_plan: 1) Simulation: integrate a simulator to replay production allocation traces and evaluate fragmentation_ratio, relocation_bytes, and p95 latency. 2) Canary: implement hole-chaining in runtime behind a feature flag; enable on a small fleet with synthetic mixed-length traffic. 3) Observability: add new metrics (free_run_count, avg_run_length, fragmentation_ratio, relocation_bytes_rate). 4) Gradual promote: roll to 10% -> 30% -> 100% after success criteria met. 5) Emergency rollback: feature flag + runtime fallback to previous allocator.
telemetry_and_criteria: Success metrics measured in canary: - fragmentation_ratio <= baseline * 0.6 after 24h - relocation_bytes_rate reduced by >= 25% - p95 latency under continuous-batching workloads improved by >= 10% - no >1% increase in OOM/eviction anomalies Observability endpoints: /metrics/kv_free_runs, /metrics/kv_avg_run_len, /logs/coalescer_activity. A/B test compares identical traffic with and without leases.
open_questions: What is the best default lease length for mixed production workloads? (initial candidates 50ms, 100ms, 200ms)
Should leases be applied only to slots under X bytes or to all sizes?
How to gracefully handle cross-GPU moves when colocated shards differ in occupancy?

acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows fragmentation_ratio drop >= 40% under representative traces
Canary meets telemetry success metrics for 72h
No regression in p99 latency beyond 2% in canary
implementation_notes: - Use compact 32-bit tags for run metadata to keep per-shard overhead low. - Coalescer should yield whenever GPU compute util > 60% for longer than 100ms. - Relocation copies must be executed in micro-batches aligned with the inference batching path to keep KV movement off the critical path. - Provide a per-tenant knob to disable leases for strict-capacity customers.
